text:
Ana: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I see a p99 regression on long-sequence workloads. Not huge but consistent.
Mike: saw the spike in the perf dashboard around the deploy window — p99 up ~35% for seq > 512. Throughput looked slightly worse too.
Priya: my hunch is KV cache thrash after kernel switches. We don't include kernel fingerprint in the cache key so when selector changes it can invalidate or create parallel keys.
Ana: quick profile dump from canary run: 
```
kernel_choice_changes_per_request: 2.9
common_kernels: ev6_fast, ev6_scalar, ev4_fallback
cache_miss_rate_after_selector: 0.42
avg_prefix_cache_lookup_ms: 1.2
```
Jordan: proposal: include kernel_tag and seq_bin in the cache key so cached KV entries are compatible with the kernel path that will consume them. Eg: `cache_key = f"{model}:{kernel_tag}:{seq_bin}:{prefix_hash}"`.
Carol: important: adding kernel_tag to keys is fine, but remember model/driver reloads. We need a namespace rotation or driver-version token so stale keys from older drivers don't collide. Otherwise we either keep old keys forever or accidentally reuse incompatible entries.
Sam: another thought — instead of increasing global cardinality we can conditionally include seq_bin only for sequences above a threshold (e.g., seq>128). Also add a short-lived driver_token stored in the driver handshake so persistence on disk can be keyed per-driver-session.
Priya: caution: seq_bin in key increases cardinality and memory pressure for popular prefixes. If we do it blindly we'll blow up cache RAM for short prefixes. Need eviction policy tweaks and a cap on new-key fanout per prefix.
Ana: ran a quick playtest where we included `kernel_tag` always but only added `seq_bin` for seq >= 256. Results: p50 ~15ms -> 14ms, p95 ~48ms -> 44ms, p99 190ms -> 140ms. Throughput +4% on our workload. Miss rate fell from 0.42 -> 0.12.
Mike: config we toggled in the canary: 
```
cache:
  key_parts: [model, kernel_tag]
  seq_bin_threshold: 256
  seq_bin_buckets: [0-255,256-511,512-1023,1024+]
  per_prefix_fanout_limit: 64
  driver_token_ttl_seconds: 86400
```
infra-bot: canary deploy started — deploy-id=deploy-2026-03-18T12:04:22Z; canary-target=engine-group-3; note: rollback hook enabled.
Carol: next steps I think are: 1) implement driver_token handshake + persistent namespace salt, 2) add conditional seq_bin injection in key builder, 3) enforce per-prefix fanout caps and monitor memory, 4) add kernel-aware unit/integration tests for hot model swaps. I'll open a PR linking this thread.
Ana: assigning owners: @Carol for driver handshake + key rotation, @Sam for cache fanout + bloom-filter idea, @Mike to validate dashboards post-rollout, @Priya to run memory/pressure stress tests.
Jordan: also add tests that simulate model hot-swap with mixed kernel versions and assert no incorrect cache reuse.
Mike: :thumbsup:
